summary: curve-plain cannot be expressed faithfully as declarative Swap JSON on the pinned 104ff465 framework. Its identity is an execution-proof admission gate: for every positive quote it probes each execution mode through a trusted executor program and requires four exact token deltas (executor debit/credit plus pool debit/credit), plus an independently observed receiver row for receiver modes and a native-input receiver probe with separately funded native ETH. The declarative identity bridge builds one variant execution program and observes only executor token balances (declarative-simulation.ts:66-80), rejects any external recipient/settlement (declarative-simulation.ts:60-62), and its receipt decoder rejects pool/receiver rows (declarative-simulation.ts:114-148). Raw effect-delta-simulation requests cannot carry a native value (adapter-request-program.ts:97-104,1377-1380; a probe value is rejected as 'unsupported field value' at adapter-request-program.ts:1817-1820), so the family's separately funded native-recipient probe cannot be reconstructed; the default native-input path is only expressible through the executor-only boundary simulation, not with the family's pool/receiver evidence. The family contract and native contract enforce those exact probe shapes (curve-plain-family/test/contract.ts:53-127 and test/native-contract.ts:237-305; test/identity-probe.ts:9-26), so a JSON cutover would either fail the unchanged family tests or silently narrow per-mode/per-direction native and recipient capability. Independent gaps also block a faithful cutover: tx-evidence nomination has no receipt-height anchor (future receipt accepted; contract.ts:486-503), declarative reverse binding never performs the MetaRegistry handler lookup (probe: verified with 0 registry calls; contract.ts:475-483), and declarative quoted fragments/actions carry no approve/transfer-to-pool requirement and only a runtimeAmountProgram node instead of the family's exchange calldata (declarative-execution.ts:1041-1044,1060-1065; contract.ts:443-465). No JSON, math registration, temporary production entry or generator run was produced; the handwritten family remains authoritative.

decisiveBlocker.capability: identity must prove, per direction and per execution mode, the trusted executor debit and receipt, the pool input/output inventory delta, the exact or 0/1-tolerance output, and the optional external/native recipient, with the same executor-program authority used by production

existingSource.fact: The quotes stage issues nativeExecutionProbe + nativeRecipientProbe for native pools and one executionProbe per ERC20 mode plus the receiver mode; every probe is optional so unknown alternatives cannot erase a complete proof.
Per positive quote it selects the first proved mode and independently proves the optional recipient mode; the direction records executionMode and recipientMode per direction.
executionProbe builds one executor-program transaction containing approve/transfer + exchange and observes executor, pool and PROBE_RECEIVER rows.

provesExecution requires exactly four token deltas: pool +amountIn, pool -amountOut, executor -amountIn, and output +amountOut to PROBE_RECEIVER for receiver modes, with the return word equal to amountOut.
provesNativeRecipient requires four observed token rows (actor + PROBE_RECEIVER), exactly one native delta equal to -amountIn on the actor, and the output row on PROBE_RECEIVER.

nativeExecutionProbe uses executor-program with executionAssetBoundary and WETH token funding; nativeRecipientProbe (106-119) uses separately funded nativeBalanceWei and four recipient/actor observations.

The contract fixture asserts probe-executor shape, then decodes every execution simulation through erc20ProbeCalls: exactly two CALL instructions, setup approve/transfer followed by one exchange, minDy equal to the quote output.
erc20ProbeCalls requires executionMode executor-program, no preCalls, exactly two ordinary CALLs and one setup + one exchange; other request shapes throw.
nativeIdentity requires executor-program probes, executionAssetBoundary undefined for receiver probes, overrideIntent.nativeBalanceWei equal to amountIn and exactly four receiver/actor token rows.
The native contract expects per-direction native-exchange-receiver capability only for the native-input direction and no recipient mode for the reverse direction.

frameworkLimitation.fact: buildDeclarativeExecutionSimulation rejects every settlement object and every recipient different from the executor: 'execution simulation requires default executor receipt'.

It hardcodes observeTokenBalances to tokenIn/tokenOut/protectedTokens with account = symbolic executor, funds exactly one tokenIn row and, for native routes, adds the central executionAssetBoundary. It cannot observe the pool or an external recipient.

decodeDeclarativeExecutionSimulationReceipt requires executor-program, no preCalls, symbolic executor-only observations, exactly one delta per observed token, positive output and zero native delta; a four-row executor+pool+receiver receipt fails with 'executor-program receipt token scope mismatch'.

Identity requests of kind declarative-execution-simulation are materialized through buildDeclarativeExecutionSimulation with the one selected variant execution definition and a JSON context; there is no per-probe recipient, target observation or native funding hook.
The effect-delta-simulation call shape is exactly caller/executionMode/to/data; there is no value field and executor-program requires centrally trusted executor code and rejects preCalls.

The handwritten identity treats an unknown alternative for one direction as unresolved for that direction only; a JSON decode would need a static optionalFailures list covering all possible dynamic execution ids and must keep the same per-direction isolation.
